rationale: The Shed Door sensor shows RSSI -88 dBm, below the -80 dBm threshold that causes intermittent disconnections. Relocating the sensor away from the metal shed (near the base station) eliminated all dropouts, confirming the metal shed is attenuating the sub-GHz signal. This is a single-device weak-signal fault, resolvable at L1 by repositioning or installing an RP-1 repeater.

repair_steps: Confirm with the customer that the Shed Door sensor remains online without dropouts when relocated away from the metal shed.
Advise the customer to either permanently reposition the sensor or base station for a clearer line of sight, or install an official RP-1 repeater to boost the signal.
Verify the sensor's RSSI is above -80 dBm after the chosen solution is implemented.
Close the case as resolved at L1.

results.text: Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.
